original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: Review-and-compose of the two open T16 owner-map PRs on the selected PR1094 supplier (PR1407, PR2077), a bounded two-stage ejection-cycle search on PR1407's map (first version of this package), a longer cycle/LNS search with a min-diff re-assignment (second version), and in this version a global class-level repack (CP-SAT pattern/flow model per (capacity, window) class, max-flow realisation) followed by the cycle/LNS loop and a class-level min-diff re-assignment toward the selected map at the same idle profile. Widths, call order, windows and both suppliers are unchanged; only owner fields of whole helper roles change.
scope_change_reason: Self-selected, not drawn by scripts/choose_research_task.py: the session started as a review of PR1407 and PR2077 and whether their moves compose (they do not: every PR2077 subset is illegal on PR1407's map). The closest catalogue card is selected-packing. The search started from an unmerged PR's map (PR1407), but the shipped map is stated and verified only against the merged selected PR1094 map; PR1407 is lineage and credit, not a dependency.
bottleneck_link: Strictly decreases the complete complex moment of the binding complex supplier while preserving rank mass 1041408, deficit 5120, the local gauge44 supplier and the 144-call chronology.
stop_rule: kappa search: stop when the session's search budget ended (gains were still coming; no stall criterion was met). Min-diff: stop when every changed class was realised and the LNS polish stalled (one gain of 5 relocations in 40 iterations, none in 3 iterations of the any-fill LNS), followed by the strict replay, the independent seed67 audit and pricing at the unchanged idle profile.
evidence: Unchanged PR1087 strict T16 replay passes all 11 stages with controls 69/12/6/15, actual_73column_sigmas 10055, kappa 0.001673054161426948 (conservative 0.001673054158574889): +2.3553e-4 relative over the selected record, +3.733e-7 over PR1407, +3.697e-7 over this package's first version (0.001672684510394236) and +3.512e-7 over its second (0.001672702955495933); 2.709% of the complex endpoint gap to the PR1240 ceiling a_hi = 0.001690054109089. Seed67 auditor R1-R7, X1, X2 and its 11 controls pass; pinned-engine pricing and the PR1069 sweep agree. The map differs from the selected PR1094 map in 1,661 rows (1,435 relocated helpers, 226 offset-only). Conditional on the selected PR1094 inherited assumptions; no open-PR dependency.
author: Philippe Van Velzen
ai_assistance: Substantial Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance: PR review, composition test, search implementation (including the global repack), min-diff re-assignment, replay and packaging. No independent human review claimed.

open_questions.question: How much further does the finite search go on this supplier's T16 owner packing?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The search was stopped while still improving; the global repack moved kappa by about 3.5e-7 where the local loop had slowed to about 1e-9 per step.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun search/loopx.sh from data/OWNERS.json.gz under a memory cap, or a new glob.py/glob5.py repack from it, strict-replay each new best, then rerun the class-level min-diff.
open_questions.blocked_by: Compute time; each new map needs the min-diff step and a strict replay again.

open_questions.question: What is the best attainable idle-residual profile for the selected supplier's T16 windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A certified bound would show how much kappa remains in owner packing at all. The class-level relaxation (search/winbound.py) only gives an uncertified surrogate ceiling (about 908.1k units in the session, roughly kappa 0.0016741), and the surrogate is only approximately linear in kappa.
open_questions.first_step: State the relaxation directly in the exact per-residual cost (or prove a kappa-surrogate inequality) and solve it to a proven bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: No certified relaxation in the exact cost exists yet; the CP-SAT bound of the surrogate relaxation did not close with one worker in 900 s.

open_questions.question: Can the diff against the selected map be made smaller at the same idle profile?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Smaller diffs are cheaper to review. The class-level relaxation implies at least 853 relocations (solver-reported), against 1,435 shipped.
open_questions.first_step: Add Gale-Ryser and pattern-change terms to search/mindiff_cls1.py so that fewer classes are unrealisable and fewer bins change pattern, then rerun mindiff_cls2.py and the LNS polish.
open_questions.blocked_by: Stage 1 is a relaxation; some classes it proposes cannot be realised and must be fixed to the selected map.
